title: Band billing names and rehearsing on the road
summary: From Don Albert and his Ten Pals to America's Greatest Swing Band; rehearsals were fitted into layoffs.

bands.name: Don Albert and his Ten Pals

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: You're talking about America's Greatest Swing Band. America's Greatest Swing Band. Well, how would those billings read? What would it say then?
Don Albert and his music. America's Greatest Swing Band.
And, of course, earlier you had another name.
Well, the first name was Don Albert and his Ten Pals.
Mm-hmm. And then his Ten Pals.
It grew into Don Albert and his Ten Pals, all 14 of them, which is a controversial name.
Mm-hmm. I guess that would attract people's attention and everything. That's right. Well, how often did you rehearse with that band?

Every time we could get a chance. You know, being a traveling band on the road and you stay up all night, you have to pick the times. And the times you were playing, maybe you had a couple of dates or you had a couple of days lay off. Well, I would call it a rehearsal and we'd rehearse that way. Or, if the guy, someone had heard an arrangement or a song they wanted to put an arrangement on, he would write it at intervals. And he'd let me know when it was ready. And, of course, I had Frank Jackie and Albert Martin and Cottrell in charge of most of the business. In fact, Cottrell was my business manager all the way through. And we would get together and see what we would call arrangements at a feasible place.
